detailed_description:
Photoreal live-action, Ferrier's farm, Utah, 1860, low side sun, deep black shadow, 35 mm film grain.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: a medium shot of two masked riders side by side on the trail, dark cloth masks under low hat brims, long rifles across the saddle bows, the moon behind the ridge rimming the horses' backs and leaving the men's faces black. The camera is on the trail level with the riders' chests, two long strides from the near horse, a 50mm lens. The moon rims the men from behind and the right. At the first frame the two riders fill the CENTRE of the frame from the bottom edge to the TOP third, the near rider at the RIGHT, the far rider at the LEFT, both masked faces a black oval under the hat brim. The two rifles lie across the middle of the frame as two lines of moonlit steel. The ridge and the white moon fill the TOP edge behind their hats. The camera pushes in on the two riders across the whole shot, travelling a forearm as the near rider lifts his rifle a hand's breadth off the saddle bow, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 the near horse's ear turns back, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:05 the camera is pushing in on the two riders across the whole shot, travelling a forearm through the last frame of the shot, and the action continues with it.

Cloth, boots, wood and glass carry the physical action, and the movement and low murmur of the people at work nearby carry under it throughout.
